A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniFlow and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, multimodal understanding, class-conditional generation, downstream vision, and ablation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds text-to-image evaluation, latent-alignment experiments, and sampling-step analyses.

M1.justification: The core self-distillation and patch-wise pixel-flow tokenizer remain unchanged. V2 adds DINOv2 latent alignment for a SigLIP2 variant and staged SANA/MMDiT adaptation with LoRA for text-to-image generation (Section 4.2 and Appendix B.3). These extend the procedure without replacing the main architecture.

E1.justification: V2 adds open-domain text-to-image generation, training on 1M synthetic image-text pairs and evaluating on GenEval and DPG-Bench. This substantially extends the previous class-conditional generation coverage. Additional face/text reconstructions extend coverage already represented in v1.

E2.justification: New Table 3 establishes a text-to-image comparison against SD v1.5, SD v2.1, PixArt-alpha, SANA, SD XL, Show-o, TokenFlow, and EMU3-Gen. Appendix comparisons additionally introduce DC-AE-f32c32 for reconstruction and VA-VAE in the latent-alignment generation experiment. The original comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 40-epoch, 256-resolution f16c32 tokenizer protocol, staged text-to-image generator training, 64-epoch LightningDiT-XL experiments, and a 1–100 Euler-step sweep. Existing configuration tables also revise AdamW beta1 from 0.5 to 0.9; this is a reported setting change, without evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds experiments testing pretrained representation choice and DINOv2 latent alignment, supported by Table 15 and PCA visualizations. Figure 21 tests reconstruction sensitivity to sampling steps. V2 also expands the teacher-encoder comparison and adds face/text reconstruction cases; the earlier distillation, loss-balance, and decoder ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or random-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new experiments retain point-estimate reporting without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises averages despite unchanged component scores: UniFlow-XL changes from 89.14 to 79.09 and TokenFlow-XL from 81.39 to 73.04. SigLIP2 reconstruction SSIM changes from 0.85 to 0.93 in v1 Table 3a/v2 Table 4a. New results include 0.65 GenEval and 84.76 DPG-Bench, plus representation, alignment, and sampling findings under newly reported settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(6) are unchanged. The added explanation of one-step reconstruction is an informal mechanism argument, without a new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the claimed average advantage over TokenFlow-XL from 7.75 to 6.05, expressed as percentages in both PDFs. The central claims of unified understanding/generation, efficient adaptation, and a win-win outcome remain.

C2.justification: V2 newly attributes generation quality to the inherited latent representation and qualifies effectiveness as dependent on the teacher encoder. It also explains one-step reconstruction through concentrated conditioning and possible numerical degradation with additional steps. The existing data-scale and fixed-resolution limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds substantial implementation information, including synthetic-data provenance, alignment stages, learning rates, step counts, and LoRA rank. V2 identifies the InternVL3-2B-Instruct checkpoint and corrects training-efficiency prose from 7k to the already-tabulated 70k steps. However, v1's repository link and availability statement are replaced by a promise to release code and data upon acceptance.

R1.justification: V2 removes the extended related-work appendix and associated references, including FlexTok and SoftVQ-VAE, while adding works supporting the new experiments, such as DC-Gen, RAE, SVG, and GenEval. The main related-work discussion and Appendix A retain substantially the same positioning against three tokenizer paradigms.

P1.justification: V2 adds a text-to-image subsection, moves the teacher-encoder discussion into Section 5, removes the detailed related-work appendix, and adds ethics and repeatability statements. Author, affiliation, and funding text also changes. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial displays for text-to-image generation, reconstruction of the new tokenizer, latent-representation comparisons, and sampling sensitivity (Tables 3, 13, 15 and Figures 4, 18, 21). It also adds face/text reconstruction figures and expands the teacher-comparison chart. Retained displays are largely preserved and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the headline aggregate comparison and strengthens generation evidence through text-to-image evaluation, latent-alignment ablations, and sampling-step analysis. These improve empirical support and interpretation. The net gain is limited by weaker documented resource access: v1 supplies a repository link and states availability, whereas v2 promises release upon acceptance.
